query: In the development of the user authentication module for the supply chain management backend, what specific technical methods did Fang Wang use to address the concurrent request token refresh issue raised by Mingzhi Li?
gold: Fang Wang uses Redis distributed locks to handle the concurrent refresh of Refresh Tokens.
context:
[1] (about=Fang Wang, episodic, t87 @2025-04-28 09:30:20) Good morning everyone. Here's an update on the user authentication module's progress: The refresh logic for Refresh Tokens has been largely implemented. Specifically, regarding the refresh issue under concurrent requests that Boss Li mentioned last week, I've handled it using a Redis distributed lock to ensure that only one request refreshes the Token at any given time, while other requests wait for the new Token to be returned. Today, I will focus on testing various invalidation and concurrency scenarios.
[2] (about=Mingzhi Li, episodic, t87 @2025-04-25 10:05:15) @Fang Wang The Token refresh mechanism must be thoroughly considered, especially the refresh issue under concurrent requests and the invalidation logic of old Tokens. @Jiayin Xu The front-end for the vendor details page's lazy loading interaction, @Ming Gu, also needs to pay attention to ensure the feasibility of subsequent development.
[3] (about=GROUP, said_by=Fang Wang, group-interaction, t136 @2025-06-09 10:22:00) Session validity 7 days; asynchronous renewal when remaining <1 day; optimistic lock for concurrency.
[4] (about=GROUP, said_by=Mingzhi Li, group-interaction, t102 @2025-05-12 14:33:21) Token refresh strategy: frontend intercepts specific status code/flag from backend response header to trigger silent refresh; solution document sent to Confluence.
agent_answer: Fang Wang addressed the concurrent-refresh issue with a **Redis distributed lock**: only one request is allowed to refresh the token at a time, while all other concurrent requests wait for the new token to be returned. The memory record also reflects the current/concurrency approach as an **optimistic lock** (with session validity of 7 days and asynchronous renewal when remaining time is under 1 day), but the specific method Fang Wang described for the concurrent refresh problem is the Redis distributed lock.
